question.prompt: Ana and Bonita were born on the same date in different years, \(n\) years apart. Last year Ana was \(5\) times as old as Bonita. This year Ana’s age is the square of Bonita’s age. What is \(n?\)

solutions.title: Model and factor the age equation
solutions.explanation:
Both girls gain one year, so using Bonita's age last year lets us express all four ages with one variable.

Let \(B\) be Bonita's age last year. Ana was then \(5B\). This year their ages are \(B+1\) and \(5B+1\), so
\[
5B+1=(B+1)^2=B^2+2B+1.
\]
Rearranging and factoring gives
\[
B^2-3B=B(B-3)=0.
\]
Thus \(B=0\) or \(B=3\). If \(B=0\), both girls would have been age \(0\) last year, contradicting their different birth years. Hence Bonita was \(3\) and Ana was \(5\cdot3=15\).

Their age difference is constant, so
\[
n=15-3=\boxed{12}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
